stem: Nodularin is a risk factor for which condition?
rationale: Small quantities of nodularin promote the formation of hepatic tumors. The ingestion of certain amino acids present in the seeds of legumes of the genus Lathyrus can result in lathyrism.

stem: Proline is converted into which substance in collagen?
rationale: In collagen, protein-bound proline and lysine residues are converted to 4-hydroxyproline and 5-hydroxylysine (Figure 3–2).

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of neurolathyrism?
rationale: Neurolathyrism, a profound neurologic disorder characterized by progressive and irreversible spastic paralysis of the legs, is caused by dietary intake of the seeds and seed products of the legume Lathyrus. Lathyrism occurs widely during famines, when Lathyrus seeds may become a major part of the diet.

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of ammonia toxicity?
rationale: The osteolathyrogen γ-glutamyl-β-aminopropionitrile (BAPN) is present in “sweet pea.” The seeds of some species also contain α,γ-diaminobutyric acid, an analogue of ornithine that inhibits the hepatic urea cycle enzyme ornithine transcarbamylase, leading to ammonia toxicity. L-β-methylaminoalanine, a neurotoxic amino acid present in Cycad seeds, has been implicated as a risk factor for neurodegenerative diseases including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis-Parkinson dementia complex in natives of Guam who consume fruit bats that feed on cycad fruit or flour made from cycad seeds.

stem: L-α-amino acids act on which substrate?
rationale: Metabolic functions of the L-α-Amino acids include the biosynthesis of urea, heme, nucleic acids, hormones such as epinephrine, and neurotransmitters such as DOPA.
